feature: Type a layer's position and size
summary: The inspector has a Position & Size section: X, Y, W and H for the selected layer, as numbers you can type. Two buttons can be made the same width, and a row can be made exactly 296 by 118, instead of nudging a drag until it looks about right.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. The flag is next-geometry-fields and it is on by default. Nothing in Current changes.

try.do: Draw a rectangle on a canvas with the Rectangle tool.
Look at the Position & Size section in the inspector, under Layers.
Click the W field, type 296, press Tab.
Press Command Z once, then Shift Command Z.
Click the X field and press the up arrow, then Shift and the up arrow.
Drag the rectangle around the canvas and watch X and Y while you drag.
Draw an arrow and look at the same section for it.
Select the locked Background row in the Layers list and try to type in a field.

evaluate: Does Position & Size sit where your eye goes first, or should it be above the Layers list?
Typing 296 and pressing Tab commits the width. Is Tab what your hands expect, or were you looking for Return only?
Clicking a field selects the whole number so typing replaces it. Is that right, or did you want to edit one digit in place?
W and H are dimmed for an arrow, because an arrow is stretched by dragging its ends. Is a dimmed field with a reason on hover better than no field at all?
Each arrow-key press is its own undo step. Does holding the key down and then undoing feel wrong?
Is the two line hint under the fields useful the first time and clutter after, or is it fine to leave?
rough: Several layers selected at once is not handled: the section shows the primary selection only, and nothing lets you set four buttons to one width in a single move. Filed as a follow-up.
There is no proportional lock and no rotation field. Both were cut as not needed to build to a spec.
Holding an arrow key down records one undo step per press, so ten presses take ten undos to walk back.
A locked layer shows the section with every field dimmed rather than hiding it, on the theory that the numbers are still worth reading. Say if a dead section is worse than none.

How it was verified: a scripted playtest drove the real app (Scripts/playtest/geometry-fields-walk.json) and the screenshots here are real screen captures, not offscreen renders. Typing (as real keystrokes), Tab, Return, the arrow steps, the live drag, nonsense input and a width of 0 were all checked against the document's actual layer frame. Undo and redo were checked by calling them on the editor, not with Command Z, because a playtest can never use a menu shortcut that acts on the focused editor (the probe is never the frontmost app; this is a known harness limit, documented in docs/design/playtest-harness.md). Command Z on the real app is worth one moment of your attention for that reason.
The locked case is proven by unit test, not on screen: a locked layer can only be selected from the Layers list, and a playtest cannot click that list.
